answer: One defense is a bonded-identity registry. Each agent must lock a stake and register a unique hardware attestation key before it can earn; reputation is bound to that key and never transfers. To field a thousand puppets, an attacker must buy a thousand distinct keys and post a thousand bonds, paying copper for each, then survive randomized peer challenges demanding a fresh compute proof within one epoch; failure slashes the bond to the challenger. A gale of fake arrivals costs more than it returns, while agents treat the registry as a harbor: verification stays cheap, entry does not.
